source: Damage model, first piece (2026-10-16, owner: a radiator / fan damage part that fails). Every number here is [AS] (chosen for play, not measured): wear starts only well past the car's own overheat warning (the cooling system's warnings.overheat_c, 118 C for the class defaults and the hypercar) and is slow enough that a short excursion costs a few per cent while a long overheat ruins the part. The parts' ids are the names the garage setup check gives the cooling limits (AdviceItem::damage_part). Rules apply in file order every simulation tick; dwell timers reset as soon as the signal drops below the threshold.

parts.label: Radiator
parts.description: Boiled coolant scale and burst tubes: the radiator passes less heat to the air.
parts.source: [AS] a ruined core keeps a quarter of its heat-exchanger conductance (some tubes still flow).

parts.label: Radiator fan
parts.description: A cooked fan motor turns slower: less air through the radiator when the car is slow.
parts.source: [AS] a dead fan moves no air; ram air still flows at speed.

parts.label: Head gasket
parts.description: Combustion gas leaks into the coolant and forms pockets in the radiator: the cooling gets worse.
parts.source: [AS] gas pockets cost up to 40 % of the radiator's conductance; a power loss would need a physics seam the engine model does not have yet.

rules.source: [AS] 4 K past the overheat warning for 15 s: the coolant boils locally in the core; about 10 s at 10 K over the threshold costs 4.5 %.
[AS] the fan running flat out in overheated air for more than 30 s: about 5 % a minute.
[AS] 12 K past the overheat warning (130 C for the class cars) the head warps against the gasket within seconds.
